item.title: Vulnerability to heat waves varies greatly from one area to another within cities
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe as a result of climate change. Heat waves are a prime example, as they have direct effects on health, thermal comfort and the livability of cities. That is why it is vital to conduct climate risk assessments to guide cities' adaptation policies and prioritize action in the most vulnerable areas.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: use the report as a planning signal — precipitation, wind, and visibility change what is safe and worth noticing. item.title: A meteor hit Oklahoma 100 million years later than scientists thought
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: ScienceDaily.
Summary: A meteor crater buried beneath Oklahoma has turned out to be nearly 100 million years younger than scientists thought. Zircon crystals show the Ames impact occurred about 370 million years ago, meaning it was not part of the mysterious Ordovician bombardment once linked to a possible ring of debris around Earth.
Waypoint’s Take: For someone heading outside, the useful question is observational: check whether the event is visible from your latitude and how moonlight interferes.
